mbq_bad_sap.description: I cut the rot out of the bark where I can. Every time I cut a soft spot away, the Sap-Blight Oozes on the Rotting Bough seep into the wound, and the rot comes back worse. I've made the same cut three times on one branch. The bark's got no chance while they're there. Clear them out so the cuts can close.
mbq_bad_sap.accept_text: They pool in the cuts I've made. Start with the fresh ones.

mbq_counting_nests.description: I count the harpies' nests for Raz'gul, so he knows how big the flock's got. I can't get close without being seen, and the last time I tried, I came back bleeding. Look into the great hollow out east on the fork, and walk the roosts along the Hollow Bough. Count every nest you see. Raz'gul won't like the number, whatever it is.
mbq_counting_nests.accept_text: Stay low on the bough, and don't stop where they can see you against the sky.

mbq_drone_cogs.description: Tel'zan will want to know how these things are built, and I want to know first. The Scuttling Gear-Drones on the Lichen Reach are full of little bronze cogs. Before the scholars in the Settlement start arguing about it, I'd like something in my hands to argue with. Bring me some of those cogs. Try not to bend them.
mbq_drone_cogs.accept_text: Pull them out whole. A bent tooth tells me nothing about the hand that cut it.

mbq_feather_knives.description: The Hollow Talons throw knives cut from their own feathers, as hard as bone. The Hollow Windcallers call up a gust behind every throw, so the knives go further than they've any right to. My scouts can't get near the hollows on the Hollow Bough, south-east of here. I need those nests counted, and nobody can count them bleeding. Take both down so my scouts can get close.
mbq_feather_knives.accept_text: Kill the Windcallers first, and the knives start falling short.

mbq_hushwing.description: There's an owl on the terraces the first climbers carved on their stones, and she's still alive, if you can believe it. She's bigger than a troll and makes no sound at all, and we call her Hushwing. She's never troubled us, but last week she took a hunter off the south terraces. Whatever's wrong with the tree, it's got into her too. Put her down.
mbq_hushwing.accept_text: You won't hear her coming. Keep looking up.

mbq_into_shriekhollow.description: With Old Raggedwing dead, I want the matron next. Matron Vyssa keeps her eyrie inside the trunk, in a hollow we call Shriekhollow, off the terraces south of Heartwatch. Every Brood-Harpy roosts on the ledges inside, and she sits at the top of the hollow's throat. Kill her, and the flock breaks. We go in while they're still arguing.
mbq_into_shriekhollow.accept_text: Climb fast and don't stop on the ledges. The brood will try to pin you there.

mbq_listening_to_the_tree.description: I hear the tree groaning at night, and I want to know where it hurts. The first climbers put their shrines where the tree's voice was loudest, so that's where to listen. Go and stand at the old shrine on the Lichen Reach, at the old tower on the south terraces, and at the far end of the Rotting Bough. Stand still at each one and listen. You'll feel it in your feet before you hear it.
mbq_listening_to_the_tree.accept_text: Don't rush between them. The tree talks slowly.

mbq_lotus_for_the_shrine.description: I lay Purple Lotus at the old shrine on the Lichen Reach, as the first climbers did. Since the rot came, it's the only offering the tree seems to take. It grows out on the boughs, if you know where to look. I'd go myself, but someone has to keep the shrine. Bring me what you can, and I'll lay it at the shrine on the Reach.
mbq_lotus_for_the_shrine.accept_text: Pick the open flowers. The tree doesn't want the buds.

mbq_moths_in_the_ropes.description: I work the top of the High Lift, and the Lichenwing Moths have been laying eggs in its ropes. The grubs that hatch eat the fibres from the inside, where you can't see the damage. One day a rope's going to go with a full basket on it. I check every rope twice a day, and I'm still finding eggs. Knock the moths out of the air along the terraces.
mbq_moths_in_the_ropes.accept_text: They come out at dusk. That's when you'll find the most of them.

mbq_notes_for_the_watch.description: I've written down everything, the spores, the splinters, and the way it goes down instead of out. Vokra's the one who'll have to go through that door one day. The tribes are going to decide what to do about the Heartwood Hollow, and she should have this before they do. I'd rather she read it than heard it secondhand. Take her my notes at Heartwatch.
mbq_notes_for_the_watch.accept_text: She'll want them more than I do. Tell her I'm sorry it isn't better news.

mbq_old_barkrot.description: There's one treant on the Rotting Bough older and bigger than the rest, and the rot spreads fastest round it. We call it Old Barkrot. It's put down roots in the worst of the rot, and it won't move unless something makes it. Every day it stands there, the rot gets a day further along the bough. I want it down.
mbq_old_barkrot.accept_text: It's rooted, so it can't chase you. Don't let that make you careless.

mbq_old_raggedwing.description: There's an old harpy on the Hollow Bough with half her feathers gone, and twice as mean as the rest. Every raid on the terraces starts with her screaming. The others call her something we can't say, and we call her Old Raggedwing. The flock follows her, and without her, they'll argue about who leads. I want her dead.
mbq_old_raggedwing.accept_text: When she screams, the flock comes. Be ready for them.

mbq_owls_on_the_terraces.description: I keep the first climbers' terraces swept, and the Mistfeather Owls nest in the old towers along them. They've started taking Heartwatch's message birds out of the air. I've got nothing against an owl, but those birds are how we talk to the city. The owls are older up here than we are, and I don't like this. Thin them out along the terraces.
mbq_owls_on_the_terraces.accept_text: Leave the towers standing. I only need fewer owls, not fewer towers.

mbq_pale_dust.description: The Lichenwing Moths along the terraces carry a pale dust on their wings. When it burns, it smells like rain, and the loa like it. I burn it at the old shrines, at every stone the first climbers left. I've run out, and the tree's been groaning till dawn. Bring me enough dust to burn at every stone on the terraces.
mbq_pale_dust.accept_text: Knock them down gently if you can. The dust comes off if you hit them too hard.

mbq_pythons_in_the_lichen.description: I watch the Lichen Reach, and the Mistcoil Pythons lie flat in the lichen, grey on grey. You don't see one until it's got your leg. I've been bitten twice this month, and I'm supposed to be watching the wreck, not my feet. I'd like to walk the Reach without counting my steps. Clear them off so I can watch in peace.
mbq_pythons_in_the_lichen.accept_text: Prod the lichen ahead of you. If it moves, it isn't lichen.

mbq_scouts_without_masters.description: I watch the wreck for Nyara. The bigger constructs walk up and down the Lichen Reach as if somebody told them to guard it and then never came back. I call them Twitching Scouts, and they spark at anything that moves. Nyara can't get near the wreck while they're there, and she's been patient longer than I would. Bring them down.
mbq_scouts_without_masters.accept_text: They spark before they strike. When you see it, step back.

mbq_sealed_for_now.description: I want you to stand at the Heartwood Hollow behind Heartwatch and listen, so you know what the watch is for. The shadow hunters sealed it, and nobody goes in until the tribes say so. It's the split behind me. Put your ear to the seal, but don't touch it. Then come back and tell me what you heard.
mbq_sealed_for_now.accept_text: Go and stand at the split behind me and put your ear to the seal. Don't touch it, only listen.

mbq_skinks_in_the_stonework.description: The Terrace Skinks dig in between the old stones to nest, and every nest they dig loosens a block the first climbers set by hand. These terraces were carried up a tree a block at a time. I've reset more stones this month than the year before. I won't lose them to lizards. Clear the skinks off the terraces.
mbq_skinks_in_the_stonework.accept_text: Kill them on the wall, not under it. I don't want to reset the blocks twice.

mbq_splinters_for_the_doctor.description: Priya's been asking for proper samples of the rot, deep ones. The Rotheart Treants on the Rotting Bough are rotten right through, so their splinters will do. I can cut rot out of bark, but I can't tell you what it is. She thinks she can, and I'd like to know. Bring the splinters to Dr. Priya Raman, not to me.
mbq_splinters_for_the_doctor.accept_text: She knows what to look for. I only know where to cut.

mbq_splints_for_the_bark.description: When I cut the rot out, I pack the hole with clean wood, so the tree grows over it instead of rotting. Thornveil is the cleanest wood on the boughs, and nothing rots it. I've used up everything I had on the last three cuts. The bough's still bleeding in places I haven't been able to pack. Bring me Thornveil wood, and I'll get to work.
mbq_splints_for_the_bark.accept_text: Cut it fresh. Thornveil that's been lying on the bark won't take.

mbq_spore_samples.description: I'm a plant pathologist from Bengaluru, and back home I'd culture the spores to find out what I'm dealing with. I haven't got a lab up here, but I've got eyes and a lot of patience. I want to see how the rot travels. The Rotspore Clouds on the Rotting Bough carry sacs of spores. Bring me some, and don't squeeze them.
mbq_spore_samples.accept_text: Carry them loose, not packed. A burst sac is no use to me.

mbq_spores_on_the_wind.description: The Rotspore Clouds drift off the Rotting Bough and settle wherever the wind drops them, and that's how the rot jumps from branch to branch. The wind's been blowing toward Heartwatch all week. The loa went quiet when the clouds came, and I haven't heard them properly since. I don't want those spores settling on the terraces. Scatter the clouds before they settle here.
mbq_spores_on_the_wind.accept_text: Hold your breath when you strike one. The spores don't care whose lungs they land in.

mbq_still_twitching.description: I came up from the Settlement to study the thing that fell out of the clouds onto the end of the Lichen Reach a month ago. It hasn't stopped moving. Little Scuttling Gear-Drones keep crawling out of it and going somewhere, and I'd very much like to know where. I can't get close while they're swarming. Go and look at it for me, and stop the drones while you're there.
mbq_still_twitching.accept_text: Watch where the drones go before you stop them. That's half of what I want to know.

mbq_talons_on_the_hollow_bough.description: The harpies came up from the coast after the merge and found the hollows in the south bough. Since they started eating the rot's grubs, every Blighted Harpy has got big and the Hollow Screechers have got loud. They lead every raid on the terraces now, and I'm tired of counting what they take. I want them to learn the terraces aren't theirs. Thin them out on the Hollow Bough.
mbq_talons_on_the_hollow_bough.accept_text: The Screechers call the others in. Take them first, and the raid falls apart.

mbq_the_climbers_names.description: I keep the names of the first climbers, cut in the stones they left up and down the terraces. Some of them are wearing away, and I'd like them read while they still can be. There's a cairn on the north terraces, the foot of the Root Stair going on up the trunk, and the old tower on the south terraces. Read me what's still there at each one. I'll cut them fresh.
mbq_the_climbers_names.accept_text: Take your time over them, because some of the names are only half there.

mbq_the_rots_heart.description: Somewhere out along the Rotting Bough, the rot's thickest. The Rotheart Treants stand in it as if they're guarding it, and they spread it further every time they move. I need to know how bad it's got, and I can't leave the watch to look myself. Find the place where it's worst. Cut the treants down while you're there.
mbq_the_rots_heart.accept_text: Look at the sap as well as the bark. If it's coming up black, tell me.

mbq_the_surveyors_core.description: Tel'zan keeps the record of everything that's fallen out of the sky, in the scholars' hall in the Great Settlement. He's going to want this more than anything he's got. Those marks inside the crystal are measurements, and every one of them is of the tree. I'd take it myself, but I want to stay with the wreck. Take it down the High Lift to the scholars' hall at the Roost.
mbq_the_surveyors_core.accept_text: Carry it wrapped. It's still warm, and I don't trust warm.

mbq_the_wakened_surveyor.description: The largest construct on the Lichen Reach woke when the wreck fell, and it's been walking the bough ever since. It turns a beam of light on the trunk and holds it there, as if it's measuring something. I call it the Wakened Surveyor. I'd like to know what it's been measuring, and I can't ask it. Stop it, and bring me back whatever's left of its core.
mbq_the_wakened_surveyor.accept_text: Don't stand in the beam. I don't know what it does to a person, and I'd rather not find out.

mbq_up_the_root_stair.description: I hear everything that comes up and down this tree. Windwarden Kazra'jin keeps Highrest, the last camp before the cloud, and he's asked Heartwatch for someone who can fight in the wind. After what you did at the Hollow, there's nobody else I'd send. Take him my knot, so he knows it's me who sent you. The Root Stair climbs the trunk above Heartwatch, and it doesn't stop till Highrest.
mbq_up_the_root_stair.accept_text: It's a long climb. Rest on the landings, because the wind gets worse the higher you go.

mbq_what_comes_up.description: I hold Heartwatch because of the Heartwood Hollow behind it. The rot climbs up out of the heartwood and spreads along the Rotting Bough, and the Blightgrubs ride it like a tide. They eat the soft wood and leave the rot room to grow, so it's spreading faster every week. Before the merge, the shadow hunters didn't come up here at all, and now we keep a watch. Go out on the bough and kill the grubs.
mbq_what_comes_up.accept_text: They're thickest where the bark's gone soft. You'll smell the place before you see it.

mbq_what_the_harpies_feed.description: I think the rot's coming from somewhere inside the trunk. The harpies in Shriekhollow carry grubs down into the hollow and drop them past the eyrie, and Scout Ree'na says they never follow. Something's at the bottom that they're feeding. Go down past the eyrie, through the Rotdark Crawlers, and find out what it is. If it's what I think, it's the thing the scouts have been calling Old Splinterheart.
mbq_what_the_harpies_feed.accept_text: Take a light. Nothing down there has seen one in a long time.

mbq_where_its_spreading.description: I need to know whether the rot's spreading out along the bough or deeper into it. Back home I'd have a field team for this, and here I've got you. I'd go myself, but the Sap-Blight Oozes out there would have me for lunch, and I'm no fighter. Go to the far end of the Rotting Bough and clear it. Then tell me what the edge of the rot looks like.
mbq_where_its_spreading.accept_text: Look at the edge closely. Which way it's going matters more than how far.
